title: The KU-barrier exponent 1/(d-1) and the moment crossover r*≈β+1 are the SAME conductor-in-the-denominator obstruction on dual faces (L^∞ vs L^{2r})
connection: KU Lemma 3.9's Wasserstein decay q^{-1/(d-1)} is vacuous because d sits in the exponent's DENOMINATOR. The moment face (subgroup_gaussSum_moment: Σ_b‖η_b‖^{2r}=q·E_r) has the char-p anomaly forced once q·E_r^{char0}<n^{2r}, crossover r*≈β+1. Dual: equidistribution needs decay ≪ε* over the support (rate ∝1/size), the moment face needs validity to depth r∝log of the norm budget (2r)^{n/2}<q (n in the exponent). Both place subgroup-size n in an exponent that q=n^β (β=O(1)) cannot beat: β·log n on the right vs n on the left. The tangent/Jacobi face (T_h at q=nm, m≈2^128) inherits the SAME structure.
why_insightful: Shows the equidistribution wall and the deep-moment-anomaly wall are not two barriers but one invariant (subgroup-size-in-exponent vs O(1)-power field) on the L^∞ (KU/Jacobi) and L^{2r} (moment) faces. Unifies W-largesieve, W-anomaly under one inequality n vs β log n.
attack_plan: Lean: size_in_exponent_obstruction parameterizing both — given budget log q=β log n and a tool needing (size)·c≤log q, derive vacuity for size=n, d=2^32. Reuse the KU omega-style proof shape with the moment threshold r_max=2 log_n p. Probe: tabulate KU rate-exponent 1/(d-1) against moment crossover r* across the same (n,q) grid to confirm they cross the budget at the same scale.
